title: Detect and backfill truncated Hosted SSE streams to prevent partial output loss
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Several mid-market customers reported that hosted API streaming responses (SSE) occasionally terminated with the last token(s) missing when clients disconnected and reconnected. Consumers observed truncated final outputs and inconsistent message IDs on resumed streams, resulting in corrupted application-level state and urgent escalations to Support. This ticket scopes triage, root-cause, fix, and rollout for Hosted; includes config mitigations for Dedicated/Private where a separate LB/proxy behavior is implicated.
steps_taken: 03-01: Triage call with Support and SRE; collected example logs and client traces from two customers (CustomerA, CustomerB).
03-02: Reproduced a disconnect/reconnect scenario in dev by terminating TCP during final chunk flush; saw difference between successful and truncated responses.
03-03: Added verbose stream-flusher traces to staging; observed race where final flush completes but connection close path drops the last chunk in the per-request lifecycle.

03-04: Compared Envoy/NLB timeouts and chunk flushing behavior between Hosted and Dedicated test clusters; Dedicated uses a managed NLB config that buffered differently which masked the bug in some cases.
root_cause: A race in the hosting runtime between the stream chunk flusher and the connection-close path. Under certain high-concurrency conditions the final chunk write completed locally but the request lifecycle cleanup advanced before the chunk was recorded to the prefix/KV cache used by stream resume. Resume tokens were tied to an in-memory sequence counter that was not persisted atomically with the last chunk, leading to non-idempotent resume tokens and dropped final chunks on reconnect.
resolution: Implement an atomic persist-and-ack step: the flusher now writes final chunk metadata to the prefix cache prior to marking the request complete. Resume tokens were changed to include a persisted sequence id and a short HMAC to ensure idempotency. Additionally, a lightweight SSE 'end-of-stream' sentinel event is emitted on both normal completion and on detected incomplete-close paths so clients can detect and request backfill. Envoy/NLB timeout recommendations for Dedicated/Private added to docs to avoid proxy-truncation masking.
code_changes_and_links: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4921 - stream-flusher: persist final-chunk before teardown
PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4929 - resume-token: include persisted-seq and HMAC
PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1187 - dashboard: streaming-truncate-alerts and per-request stream-seq metrics
rollout_plan: Patch to runtime-1.19 (canary channel): deploy to 1% Hosted traffic with canary tracing on 2026-03-11.
Monitor canary for 48h for truncated-stream-rate (goal: < 1e-4 per 10k streams) and for resume-success-rate improvement.
If stable, expand to 25% on 2026-03-13 and to 100% on 2026-03-15 for Hosted.
Submit configuration guidance for Dedicated/Private customers; ops-runbook for on-prem teams to tune proxy timeouts and apply shim if they use older runtime versions.
Backport hotfix to runtime-1.18 and runtime-1.17 for enterprise Dedicated customers with active SLA (track via patch backport PRs).
monitoring_and_alerts: New alert: streaming.truncation_rate > 1e-3 for 10m -> P0 paging to SRE + Eng oncall.
Dashboard: per-model and per-region SSE resume-success-rate, truncated-stream-rate, and average time-to-persist-final-chunk.
Added sampling of raw SSE payloads (PII-stripped) for 0.1% of requests to assist debugging when truncation is reported.
testing_and_validation: Unit tests for resume-token generation and verification (HMAC).
Integration tests that simulate abrupt TCP close during last-chunk flush and assert that resume returns complete transcript.
Load test in staging with 10k concurrent SSE clients and randomized disconnects to validate the fix under stress.
SDK: add client-side backoff and explicit resume-request when end-of-stream sentinel missing for 3s after last SSE event.
deployment_status: Canary deployed 2026-03-11 to 1% Hosted; initial metrics show truncated-stream-rate dropped by 92% vs baseline. No increase in latency or error-rate observed. Preparing 25% rollout pending 48h steady state. Backport PRs opened for Dedicated partner tenants.
post_release_followups: Write short postmortem summarizing timeline, detection, root cause, and corrective actions (owner: Aisha Patel).
Add a test to CI that fails if resume-token loses idempotency semantics.
Coordinate with Account Management to notify affected customers of fix and recommended client SDK upgrade to pick up sentinel/backfill handling.
Plan a small performance regression check in runtime-1.20 to ensure persist-on-final-chunk does not add measurable CPU cost at 99th percentile.
Schedule a knowledge-share with Dedicated/Private field engineering to walk through proxy timeout guidance and backport plan.
